([[The Villages, Florida]]) | college = [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] (2019–2021) | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] – Coaches (2021) * Second-team All-SEC – [[Associated Press|AP]] (2021) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2019]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2019) }} '''Tre'Shaun Mann''' (born February 3, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]]. ==High school career== Mann played basketball for [[The Villages Charter Schools]] in [[The Villages, Florida]]. As a junior, he averaged 20 points and 5.6 rebounds per game, and suffered a [[meniscus tear|torn meniscus]] in his right knee at the Class 5A-District 5 title game.{{cite web |last1=Jolley |first1=Frank |title=The Villages Tre Mann working to raise his game |url=https://www.dailycommercial.com/sports/20180630/villages-tre-mann-working-to-raise-his-game |website=[[Daily Commercial]] |access-date=July 24, 2021 |date=June 30, 2018}} In his senior season, Mann averaged 23.6 points and 4.9 rebounds per game, and was named ''[[Daily Commercial]]'' All-Area Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Jolley |first1=Frank |title=The Villages’ Mann is DC boys hoops Player of the Year |url=https://www.dailycommercial.com/sports/20190421/villages-mann-is-dc-boys-hoops-player-of-year |website=[[Daily Commercial]] |access-date=July 24, 2021 |date=April 21, 2019}} He was selected to play in the [[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Ryan |title=Tre Mann is Florida Hoop Royalty |url=https://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/tre-mann-story/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |access-date=July 24, 2021 |date=June 11, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Mann was considered a five-star recruit by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], and a four-star recruit by [[ESPN]]. On August 28, 2018, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{cite web|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2793131-4-star-guard-tre-mann-commits-to-florida-over-north-carolina|title=5-Star Guard Tre Mann Commits to Florida over North Carolina|first=Alec|last=Nathan|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=August 28, 2018|accessdate=April 19, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Tre Mann | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Gainesville, Florida|Gainesville, FL]] | highschool = [[The Villages Charter Schools|The Villages]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 4 | weight = 185 | 40 = | commitdate = August 28, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 89 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = Florida 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 Florida Gators Recruiting Class | rivals school = florida | scout s = | espn schoolid = 57 | 247 overall = 12 | rivals overall = 24 | espn overall = 33 | accessdate = April 5, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== In his first game in a Florida uniform, Mann had 11 points and four rebounds as the Gators defeated [[North Florida Ospreys men's basketball|North Florida]] 74–59.{{cite news |title=Blackshear gets double-double, No. 6 Florida beats UNF 74-59 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169796 |accessdate=November 5, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} He averaged 5.3 points per game as a freshman. Following the season he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=Florida guards Andrew Nembhard and Tre Mann declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29101274/florida-guard-andrew-nembhard-declares-nba-draft-again |accessdate=April 27, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 26, 2020}} On July 7, 2020, Mann announced he was returning to Florida, in part due to the possibility to start at point guard.{{cite news |title=Florida's Tre Mann returning for chance to start |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29424312/florida-tre-mann-returning-chance-start |accessdate=July 8, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=July 7, 2020}} In his sophomore season debut on December 2, 2020, Mann scored 19 points in a 76–69 win against [[Army Black Knights men's basketball|Army]].{{cite news |title=Mann scores 19, Florida opens season by topping Army 76–69 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401266615 |access-date=December 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 2, 2020}} On March 12, 2021, he scored a career-high 30 points in a 78–66 loss to [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] at the [[2021 SEC Men's Basketball Tournament|SEC Tournament]] quarterfinals.{{cite web |title=Tre Mann’s 30 points not enough as Gators lose to Tennessee in SEC quarterfinal |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-gators/os-sp-uf-tennessee-sec-tournament-0313-20210312-epmtz2xdyvdwnmgr3ufv4bfvju-story.html |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |publisher= [[Associated Press]]|access-date=July 24, 2021 |date=March 12, 2021}} As a sophomore, Mann averaged 16 points, 5.6 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.4 steals per game, and was named First Team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) by the league's coaches and Second Team All-SEC by the media. On March 24, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Florida Gators sophomore Tre Mann declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31126656/florida-sophomore-tre-mann-declares-nba-draft |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 24, 2021 |date=March 24, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] | '''29''' || 4 || 17.8 || .356 || .275 || .655 || 1.9 || .7 || .6 || '''.1''' || 5.3 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] | 24 || '''24''' || '''32.4''' || '''.459''' || '''.402''' || '''.831''' || '''5.6''' || '''3.5''' || '''1.4''' || '''.1''' || '''16.0''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 53 || 28 || 24.4 || .422 || .349 || .788 || 3.6 || 1.9 || .9 || .1 || 10.2 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://floridagators.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=11713 Florida Gators bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Mann, Tre}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Florida]] [[Category:Florida Gators men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Gainesville, Florida]]
